mappings.note: Parts (a), (b) and (d) are saturation and its temperature dependence (LO-8); part (c) is a standalone m/m calculation (LO-7) that shares nothing with them. Two codes because the concentration sum is genuinely a second topic bolted onto the item.

Separating funnel, its density principle, and then the sharp extension -- two immiscible liquids of EQUAL density cannot be separated by it. That extension is the cleanest test in the chapter of LO-11's 'justifies the choice from the properties of the mixture'.

Simple distillation apparatus and principle, then why it fails on crude petroleum. LO-10 carries both simple and fractional distillation plus the choice between them, so one code covers all three parts.

Parts (a), (b) and (d) are the Tyndall effect and the dispersed phase and medium of clouds (LO-15); part (c) asks for colloid versus suspension on size and settling, which is LO-14 stated outright. Both clearly earned.

The single best match to LO-13 in the chapter: mechanism of centrifugation, its medical use, and then water that is STILL cloudy after filtration being cleared by coagulation -- which is LO-13's sentence in full, filtration failing and coagulation chosen instead.
Crude oil fractions, how fractional distillation differs from simple in its application window, and why petroleum needs it. LO-10's appropriateness clause across all three parts.

A stapled-together item: part (a) is a % v/v calculation (LO-7), part (b) is emulsions and emulsifying agents (LO-15). The two halves share no content, so both codes are cited rather than picking the larger half.

Stage fog versus a clear sports drink: part (a) is a homogeneous/heterogeneous classification (LO-6) and parts (b) and (c) are the Tyndall effect and why a solution shows none (LO-15). LO-14 is not added because the reasoning stays at 'large enough to scatter' without invoking the nanometre bands.

PARTLY POOR FIT, fourth appearance of the % m/V gap. Part (a), naming glucose as solute and water as solvent, is squarely LO-7; part (b) is a mass-by-volume calculation, a unit LO-7 does not list. Cited once as nearest, with the gap recorded.

The halwai's syrup: parts (a) and (b) are saturation and rising solubility with temperature (LO-8), part (c) is sugar crystallising out as the vat cools overnight (LO-9). This is the one item where slow cooling to crystals and the saturation definition are both assessed.

Names the separating funnel, explains the oil-on-top density order, and describes draining the lower layer -- LO-11 throughout. Part (a)'s 'heterogeneous mixture of two immiscible liquids' is the premise of LO-11 rather than a separate LO-6 classification task, unlike the fog-and-sports-drink item where the classification stands alone.
Vanishing naphthalene balls with no wet stains, the definition of sublimation, and then using it to separate crushed naphthalene from another solid -- both clauses of LO-12 in one everyday case.

Forensic ink analysis: names paper chromatography, infers that black ink is a mixture, and attributes separation to differing interaction with solvent and paper. LO-11's principle clause applied to an unfamiliar context.

Names distillation, justifies it from miscibility and a gap greater than 25 degrees, and predicts acetone vaporises first. LO-10. Recovering BOTH liquids is what makes distillation rather than evaporation the answer, which is still inside LO-10.

Parts (a), (b), (d) and (e) are centrifugation and alum coagulation (LO-13); part (c) asks how blood is classified, which is LO-14's three-way distinction. Cited together because the classification question is answered from particle behaviour, not from the spin.

Paneer making: lemon juice as coagulant, then muslin-cloth filtration of the curds. LO-13 owns coagulation, and the filtration here is the ordinary kind that works once the particles have been clumped -- which is the positive side of the same outcome. Milk's emulsion nature is background and not asked, so not LO-15.

Sea-salt purification: geometric crystals named, crystallisation identified, hot filtration justified, and crystallisation preferred over evaporation to dryness. LO-9's principle, regular-solid description and purity consequence, all in one item.
